case_title: State of M.P. v. Ashok & Others Etc.
accused_victim_relationship: Prior enmity/dispute: the victim's statement describes an old enmity and quarrel with Dibbu and others; no separate relationship with the respondents is described
statutory_provisions: IPC s.302 r/w s.149; IPC s.147
weapon: Sword (thrown by a co-accused, Harilal) and burning tyre (thrown by respondent Vidhna); petrol and matchstick were used by other accused
evidence_type: Dying declarations (written statements Ext. P-20 and P-17 and oral declarations); eyewitness testimony (PW13); medical (post-mortem report)
aggravating_circumstances: Group waited in ambush, surrounded the victim to prevent escape while he was burning, and threw a burning tyre and a sword at him
trial_court_outcome: Convicted under s.302 r/w s.149 IPC (life imprisonment) and s.147 IPC (6 months RI); co-accused Dibbu and Jittu convicted under s.302 (life) and s.148 (1 year RI)
high_court_outcome: Respondents' appeals allowed and acquitted of all charges (benefit of doubt); conviction of Dibbu and Jittu affirmed; appeals of Harilal and Banshilal abated on death
offence_finally_established: IPC s.302 read with s.149 (murder by unlawful assembly); IPC s.147
neutral_facts: The victim was riding home from work on a bicycle at about 8:00 p.m. on the evening of the incident, with his younger brother following about 10 to 15 feet behind. At a spot in front of a house, one man stopped the victim by catching his bicycle and poured petrol over him, and another man set him alight with a matchstick. The victim began burning and ran from the spot. A group of persons surrounded him, shouting that he should be beaten, burned and not allowed to escape. One member of the group threw a burning tyre onto him, and another threw a sword at him as he ran. The victim ran to a neighbouring house, where the fire was put out. The brother ran home to alert the family, and relatives came to the scene before the victim was taken to hospital. Before dying, the victim gave two statements, one recorded at the hospital by a police officer and one recorded by an Executive Magistrate after a doctor certified he was conscious. Both named the persons involved and described the group's role and an earlier enmity with the main assailants. The brother testified as an eyewitness. The post-mortem recorded burns over about 90% of the body and an incised wound on the back of the chest. The victim died the following day. After investigation, a charge sheet was filed against ten persons and twenty prosecution witnesses were examined.
physical_harm: Death of the victim on 12.04.1989 from burns (about 90% third-degree burns); incised wound on the back of the chest
number_of_offences: 2 charged; 2 finally upheld (s.302 r/w s.149 and s.147)
premeditation_planning: Court found the group was waiting in ambush and showed preparedness (one carried a sword); no express finding of premeditation as such
motive: alleged: revenge for an old enmity and quarrel (as stated by the victim); the Court did not separately decide motive
key_evidence_accepted: Dying declarations Ext. P-20 and Ext. P-17 (consistent, naming the accused and their roles); eyewitness testimony of PW13; post-mortem incised injury on the back consistent with PW13's account
witness_credibility: Court accepted PW13 as an eyewitness; the High Court had not disbelieved his testimony; the Court found the High Court's view against the record
trial_duration: offence: 11.04.1989; trial judgment: not given; High Court: 11.01.2007; Supreme Court: 01.07.2015
legal_representation: For the State (appellant): Vanshaja Shukla, Mishra Saurabh. For the respondents: Akshat Shrivastava, Sarabjit Dutta
investigation_status: FIR registered (Dehati Nalishi Ext. P-20); investigation completed; charge sheet filed against 10 accused; 20 prosecution witnesses examined, 3 defence witnesses examined
appeal_history: Trial court: all 10 convicted (life for murder). High Court: conviction of Dibbu and Jittu affirmed; respondents acquitted; Harilal and Banshilal's appeals abated on death. Supreme Court: State's appeals allowed, acquittal set aside, conviction restored for respondents
prosecution_argument: Role of respondents was established by dying declarations and eyewitness testimony; the post-mortem injury supported the eyewitness account; the High Court's view was unsustainable
defence_argument: Principal role in the dying declarations was not attributed to the respondents, so the High Court rightly gave them benefit of doubt
legal_principle_applied: Membership of unlawful assembly under s.149 IPC inferred from presence, preparedness and participation, acting in concert with a common object; appellate court should be slow to interfere with acquittal but may do so where the assessment is against the record
judicial_aggravating_factors: Active role in the attack (throwing burning tyre and sword); readiness with a sword; encircling the victim so he could not escape
other_sentence_order: Respondents directed to be taken into custody forthwith; proceedings abated against respondent no.6 (Surendra) on death

accused_victim_relationship.quote: There is an old enmity and quarrel was going on between us and Dibbu etc.

offence_category.quote: Penal Code, 1860: s. 302 rlw s. 149 - Murder

evidence_type.quote: Dying declarations namely statements Exts.P-20 and P-17, so also oral declarations as deposed by PWs 4 and 15 and the eye-witness account through PW13 were principally relied upon by the prosecution.

aggravating_circumstances.quote: The sequence of narration certainly shows that they were waiting in ambush.

trial_court_outcome.quote: All the other accused were sentenced to life imprisonment under section 302 read with section 149 I.P.C. and to rigorous imprisonment for 6 month under section 147 I.P.C.

high_court_outcome.quote: The High Court however gava benefit of doubt to the respondents on the premise that they had reached the spot after the commission of offence

final_outcome.quote: We therefore allow these appeals, set-aside the judgment and order of acquittal rendered by the High Court and restore the judgment of conviction and sentence

offence_finally_established.quote: restore the judgment of conviction and sentence as recorded by the trial Court against the respondents.

imprisonment_type.quote: All the other accused were sentenced to life imprisonment under section 302 read with section 149 I.P.C.

neutral_facts.quote: Both were coming on bicycles, PW13 being 10-15 feet behind said Tikaram.

attempt_completion.quote: On 12.04.1989 at about 8:15 p.m. Tikaram succumbed to his injuries.

number_of_offences.quote: All the other accused were sentenced to life imprisonment under section 302 read with section 149 I.P.C. and to rigorous imprisonment for 6 month under section 147 I.P.C.

premeditation_planning.quote: The sequence of narration certainly shows that they were waiting in ambush.

motive.quote: For taking revenge from the said enmity today they poured petrol on me and set on fire, in order to kill me.

key_evidence_accepted.quote: Statement Ext. P-20 leading to the registration of crime as well as statement Ext. P-17 recorded by the Executive Magistrate are dying declarations by Tikaram.

witness_credibility.quote: Having gone through the record we find the presence of said PW13 completely established and accept him to be eye witness to the occurrence.

trial_duration.quote: On 12.04.1989 at about 8:15 p.m. Tikaram succumbed to his injuries.

legal_representation.quote: Vanshaja Shukla, Mishra Saurabh for the Appellant. Akshat Shrivastava, Sarabjit Dutta for the Respondents.

investigation_status.quote: After due investigation charge sheet was filed and 10 accused persons were sent for trial.

appeal_history.quote: The judgment to the extent it acquitted the present respondents of all the offences is presently under challenge at the instance of the State of Madhya Pradesh in these appeals by special leave.

prosecution_argument.quote: the role of the present respondents in the commission of crime was clearly made out from the dying declarations as well as from the testimony of the eye witness.

defence_argument.quote: It was submitted that the principal role as alleged in the dying declarations was not as regards the present respondents and as such they were rightly granted benefit of doubt by the High Court.

legal_principle_applied.quote: Even if one of them was ready with a sword, that is clearly indicative of the level of preparedness on their part and we see no reason how they could not be said to bie members of unlawful assembly.

judicial_aggravating_factors.quote: Further, throwing of burning tyre and the sword would also indicate the active role played by them.

other_sentence_order.quote: The respondents shall be taken in custody forthwith to serve the sentence awarded to them.
